$comment: THE RULED PATH (R7), WRITTEN DOWN WHERE A GATE CAN READ IT.
Finding 106, 2026-08-24. Case Q proved two correct credentials and let them
point at a public-internet PostgreSQL host, because the predicate accepted
any of Cloudflare's three origin variants as long as CONTROL and JOBS agreed.
R7 is more specific than that:
Worker -> Hyperdrive -> Workers VPC Service -> Cloudflare Tunnel -> Pigsty
The Hyperdrive configuration names only a service_id, so everything R7
actually rules — which tunnel, which host, which port, what TLS — lives on
the VPC Service object one level down, and has to be compared against an
EXPECTED value. This file is that value.
WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE. Finding 105: an attestation
whose subject is caller-chosen is a capability to attest the wrong system. The
same is true of its expected VALUES — a gate handed both the subject and the
expectation by its caller proves only that the caller was self-consistent. A
ruling belongs in the tree, under review, in a diff.
NOTHING IS PROVISIONED. Every value below is a placeholder, deliberately not a
plausible-looking real one, for the same reason wrangler.toml's ids are: an id
that looked real could be copied into a deploy by mistake. Creating the tunnel
and the VPC Service is a spend decision and belongs to Travis
(agents/C-infrastructure.md).
$hostVariantComment: FINDING 125, 2026-08-24. The ruling now names WHICH of Cloudflare's host
variants the service must be — ipv4 | ipv6 | dual_stack | hostname — because
the predicate used to read `host.ipv4 ?? host.ipv6 ?? host.hostname` and take
the first one present. REPRODUCED: a dual-stack service carrying the expected
ipv4 and an entirely unreviewed ipv6 passed, reporting only the ipv4. Proving
one target matches is not proving these are all the targets.
$certVerificationComment: The TLS policy is a RULING, not a preference, and it lives here because the
code used to say one thing in a comment and enforce another: the note read
'acceptable for an IP target with a private CA' while accepting verify_ca for
a HOSTNAME target too, which is the one case where skipping the hostname
check matters most. verify_full is required unless this file says otherwise,
and 'disabled' is refused even if this file asks for it.
$portComment: 5432 is not a placeholder. It is the PostgreSQL port and the VPC Service's
tcp_port must be it; a service on another port is not the database this
